title: Text clients got more to work with
summary:
The text API gained more ways to work with models while its streaming and provider plumbing became less surprising.

The API added function calling, provider-backed streaming, an o1-mini option, and a larger 512,000-character limit for OpenAI text requests. SearchGPT can also use an explicitly supplied model. These changes give clients more control over both what they ask for and how they receive it.

The first pass at streaming was followed by fixes for SSE formatting, error responses, and cached-stream replay. Response handling was then simplified to emit a single SSE [DONE] event. Streaming is useful; making clients guess whether a chunk is an event is less useful.

OpenAI-backed requests moved to a gateway client, while Cloudflare text generation switched to its OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint. Shared-client changes remove null fields from requests, avoid an unsupported Cloudflare seed parameter, and add a default system prompt only when one is configured. Existing OpenAI aliases still map to their Azure deployments.

PrivatePollenAI, Gacha, and Musify joined the listings, spanning local-first chat, a social bot, and music tools. Project links and author profiles also got more flexible, and urSapere AI’s listing was updated.
